transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 37 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Grace Lawson (Tidewater PM), Dr. Omar Patel (Head of Data), Leah Kim (Security), Marcus Reed (ML Eng)

Summary:
- Quick review of latest quality metrics; small regressions observed in intent extraction and hallucination rate on medications prompts.
- Decided to update prompt variants, tighten guardrails (entity whitelist/blacklist), and re-run targeted evals.
- Security team requested SOC2 artifacts and network diagram for private deployment evaluation.

Topics:
- Quality metrics and scoring rubric (precision/recall, F1, hallucination rate)
- Guardrail tuning (regex/entity lists, confidence thresholds)
- Regression triage and next steps
- Security and deployment constraints (VPC, KMS)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off um quick agenda, go over the eval results, triage the failing prompts, and agree next steps.
[00:08] Grace Lawson: sounds good, thanks Maya. we only have 30 minutes so let's try to be tight.
[00:15] Daniel Park: quick note, i ran the nightly evals yesterday after the new prompt variants and we saw a drop in intent extraction on the meds subset, about a 6% F1 hit, so we'll walk through that.
[00:30] Marcus Reed: yeah we noticed that in our end-to-end tests too, the model sometimes merges dose and frequency into a single entity which breaks our downstream mapping.
[00:45] Dr. Omar Patel: can you show us the exact examples? is this only with long context or also short notes?
[00:53] Daniel Park: primarily long clinical notes > 900 tokens, we suspect the KV cache behavior and also the prompt prefix ordering is changing context salience. i think there's an interaction with the prompt that used the phrase "current medications" followed by a list.
[01:10] Grace Lawson: okay, that matches our repro. sometimes the model outputs compound entities like "50 mg twice daily" as a single span.
[01:22] Maya Chen: got it. just to set expectations, the current pilot is on Redwood Hosted API but you're evaluating Dedicated/Private options later for compliance, right?
[01:33] Leah Kim: correct. security wants to understand encryption at rest and KMS integration before we move to dedicated. also audit logs.
[01:42] Maya Chen: we'll send SOC2 and a network diagram; Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM via integrations, we'll include details in the packet.
[01:55] Leah Kim: perfect.
[02:00] Daniel Park: back to the regression: i compared the top 50 failing prompts, about 12 consistently fail across runs. many are med-list extraction or medication intent prompts. i think a fix path is twofold: tweak prompt ordering and add entity-level guardrails (whitelist of dosage units, separators).
[02:20] Marcus Reed: could you add an explicit instruction like "separate dosage frequency and amount into distinct fields"? we tried that but the model sometimes ignores it.
[02:31] Daniel Park: yes, and we can also enforce a post-run parser with stricter heuristics to catch merged spans. the tradeoff is more post-processing complexity.
[02:45] Grace Lawson: we prefer minimal post-processing if we can get the model to be more consistent, but we'll accept some parsing as a guardrail. what's the plan for scoring?
[02:55] Maya Chen: right now the scoring rubric weights entity-level precision more heavily for meds (0.6) and intent accuracy 0.4; we can shift weights temporarily while we iterate.
[03:10] Dr. Omar Patel: can you show examples of the model outputs vs. ground truth?
[03:16] Daniel Park: sure, i pasted five failing cases in the shared drive link, one quick example: input clinical note includes "She takes lisinopril 10mg once daily and metformin 500 mg twice a day". Model output: "lisinopril 10mg once daily metformin 500 mg twice a day" as a single medication entity; ground truth expects two medication entities with dose/frequency split.
[03:40] Marcus Reed: that kind of merging kills our mapping to RxNorm IDs.
[03:45] Daniel Park: exactly. one mitigation is to separate with explicit separators in the prompt like "--MEDICATIONS--" before the list, or force a JSON output schema with fields for name, dose, frequency.
[03:58] Grace Lawson: forcing JSON output helped earlier but we saw some hallucination in slots that were empty.
[04:06] Daniel Park: yeah, sometimes the model invents a dosage if it's uncertain. adding a required confidence field and a threshold to set empty when below thresh helps.
[04:18] Dr. Omar Patel: what about temperature and sampling? are you running at lower temp for these prompts?
[04:25] Daniel Park: for meds we run 0.0-0.2; the nightly eval used 0.1. the regression seemed independent of temp, more tied to prompt ordering and the large context.
[04:36] Maya Chen: curious, are you running with caching or without during eval?
[04:40] Marcus Reed: we ran both, similar results. might be an interaction with the KV cache when the sequence length is long, like Daniel mentioned.
[04:48] Daniel Park: small nit, sometimes the transcripting here spells KV as K V cache in logs, but it's the same.
[04:55] Grace Lawson: (laughs) noted.
[05:00] Maya Chen: okay action plan proposal: 1) Daniel will prepare three prompt variants focusing on separators, required JSON schema with nullable slots, and explicit entity extraction instructions. 2) We'll add a parser-based guardrail as a safety net. 3) Re-run regression on meds subset and share CSV. 4) Security gets SOC2 and network diagram. does that align?
[05:22] Leah Kim: yes please include KMS/HSM notes and where logs are stored and retention.
[05:28] Maya Chen: noted.
[05:30] Grace Lawson: quick Q on scoring: can we surface per-prompt breakdown so we can prioritize fixes?
[05:36] Daniel Park: yes we already have per-prompt metrics i'll attach the top failing list and a heatmap; it's in the shared folder.
[05:44] Marcus Reed: another ask: can we try a stronger guardrail that rejects output when the entity span doesn't match a dosage pattern? like a regex enforce.
[05:54] Daniel Park: yep that's part of the parser guardrail. we can run heuristic checks first, then only accept model output if it passes. otherwise fallback to a structured extractor.
[06:06] Dr. Omar Patel: does Redwood support deterministic kernels or compilation modes that reduce variance? previously we saw slight output variance across runs.
[06:16] Maya Chen: the runtime has deterministic modes for token sampling and KV cache alignment in Dedicated deployments; we can share notes. in Hosted API it's mostly low-variance but Dedicated gives more control over compilation and kernels.
[06:32] Leah Kim: that's good to know for compliance.
[06:35] Maya Chen: on pricing, moving to Dedicated will change unit economics; i'll send options in the pricing sheet.
[06:43] Marcus Reed: are there any known regressions from last week's model version bump?
[06:47] Daniel Park: we upgraded a quantization profile last week for perf; that shouldn't affect semantics but it looks like a prompt ordering interaction created this regression. i'm marking it as medium priority.
[07:00] Grace Lawson: can you clarify how you run regression tests? we want to reproduce locally.
[07:05] Daniel Park: we keep a canonical prompt set and run batch evals across model variants; the eval records per-prompt F1/precision/recall, hallucination counts, and a JSON diff. i'll send the instructions to reproduce and the eval runner commands.
[07:18] Grace Lawson: please include versions and exact API parameters, headers, gating flags. Marcus will want to run locally.
[07:24] Marcus Reed: yes i'll take that.
[07:26] Daniel Park: ok i'll include the --no-cache and --use-cache flags examples.
[07:30] Maya Chen: security wise, Leah, anything else besides SOC2 and KMS?
[07:36] Leah Kim: SSO/SAML support for console access, RBAC mapping to our roles, and long-term retention policy. we currently home data retention at 90 days for PII, but need to map to your retention.
[07:50] Maya Chen: Redwood Console supports RBAC and SSO; retention is configurable in Private deployments. we'll include defaults and options in the doc set.
[07:58] Leah Kim: also need a pointer to where transcript logs store PII redaction options.
[08:05] Daniel Park: we have a redaction layer and can run PII scrubbing pre-storage; i'll include an example config.
[08:12] Grace Lawson: quick check: are we blocking any model families? we tried Anthropic earlier as a baseline.
[08:18] Maya Chen: you can pick from catalog; we have Redwood-curated open models and you can route by policy. no hard blocks.
[08:26] Dr. Omar Patel: another minor regression we saw: free-text summarization hallucinated a non-existent allergy in one case.
[08:34] Daniel Park: noted that's a hallucination issue, likely due to prompt leakage in long context. adding an explicit 'do not invent' instruction plus a low temperature helps.
[08:45] Grace Lawson: for the immediate triage, what's the timeline?
[08:49] Maya Chen: propose tasks and timeline: prompt variants and guardrail implement by 2026-04-09, regression re-run 2026-04-12, security packet by 2026-04-10, follow-up sync week of 2026-04-13.
[09:03] Marcus Reed: that works from our side.
[09:07] Leah Kim: please send SOC2 scope (Type II?) and clarify what controls are covered.
[09:14] Maya Chen: will do, Type II docs included.
[09:18] Daniel Park: quick note on scoring tweak: we can temporarily lower the intent weight and up entity precision to see if that reduces false positives on meds, then revert once fixed. we'll record the deltas.
[09:29] Grace Lawson: that seems reasonable. remember we still care about intent mapping for downstream decisioning.
[09:35] Maya Chen: absolutely.
[09:37] Daniel Park: final point, i'll add a guardrail that returns an explicit "unsure" or null when confidence is below 0.65 to avoid hallucinated doses.
[09:47] Marcus Reed: yes please, we'd prefer a null than made-up data.
[09:51] Maya Chen: ok, we'll wrap up. any last questions?
[09:55] Grace Lawson: no, thanks everyone.
[10:00] Maya Chen: recap of next steps... Daniel to share prompt variants and eval CSV, Maya to send security and pricing, Marcus to provide additional failure cases. meet same time next week. thanks.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcription and name misspellings (e.g., "K V cache" vs KV cache), speaker overlap present.
